title: Cochain complexes of sheaves of modules on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A *cochain complex* $\mathcal F^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules consists of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F^i$, $i\in\mathbf Z$, and morphisms $d^i:\mathcal F^i\to\mathcal F^{i+1}$ of $\mathcal O$-modules with $d^{i+1}\circ d^i=0$ for all $i$. A *morphism of cochain complexes* $f:\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a family of morphisms $f^i:\mathcal F^i\to\mathcal G^i$ of $\mathcal O$-modules with $d^i_{\mathcal G}\circ f^i=f^{i+1}\circ d^i_{\mathcal F}$ for all $i$. These form a category $\mathrm{CoCh}(\Mod(\mathcal O))$, which is abelian.

source.place: Section 010V (homology-section-complexes), definition of cochain complexes and the category CoCh(A); Lemma 0114 (homology-lemma-cat-cochain-abelian): CoCh(A) is abelian; applied to A = Mod(O) as in literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex Section 06YL
